definition: A person whose partner or close family member has been neurologically altered by BCI damage, geneware failure, or ELF interference to the point of fundamental personality change — present in body but absent in identity. Distinct from literal death but carries parallel grief.
origin: Medical community euphemism that crossed into common usage; resonance refers to the neural resonance profiles used to identify individuals
usage: All tiers; counseling services use it clinically, communities use it with compassion, and insurance firms use it to classify dependency claims
example: There's a support group in the Lakeshore district for resonance widows — people who lost someone who is still technically breathing.
